q24197.en: The symbol shown is on the switch that turns on the main beam headlights.

explain.short: The straight horizontal lines mean main beam. 'Proiettori di profondità' is another name for the main beam (abbaglianti).
explain.rule: Straight lines = main beam (abbaglianti, 'proiettori di profondità'). The symbol is on its switch and on a blue light.
explain.trap: 'proiettori di profondità' sounds strange, but it simply means the main beam (abbaglianti).

sceneParams.caption: Straight lines: main beam switch

q24198.en: The symbol shown is on a blue warning light.

explain.short: When the main beam is on, a blue light with this symbol switches on in the dashboard. Blue is used only for the main beam.
explain.rule: Straight lines = main beam (abbaglianti, 'proiettori di profondità'). The symbol is on its switch and on a blue light.
explain.trap: 'luce blu' is right: the main beam light is blue, the dipped beam light is green.

sceneParams.caption: Main beam on: the warning light is blue

q24199.en: The symbol shown is on a green warning light.

explain.short: This is the main beam symbol, and its warning light is blue, not green. Green is for the dipped beam.
explain.rule: Straight lines = main beam (abbaglianti, 'proiettori di profondità'). The symbol is on its switch and on a blue light.
explain.trap: 'verde' is the trap: green belongs to the dipped beam (lines sloping down), not to this symbol.

sceneParams.caption: Not green: the main beam light is blue
lines: Its light is BLUE, not green

q24200.en: The symbol shown is on the switch that turns on the dipped beam headlights.

explain.short: Straight horizontal lines mean main beam. The dipped beam symbol has lines sloping down towards the road.
explain.rule: Straight lines = main beam (abbaglianti, 'proiettori di profondità'). The symbol is on its switch and on a blue light.
explain.trap: 'anabbaglianti' (dipped beam) is the trap: this symbol is the 'abbaglianti' (main beam).

sceneParams.caption: Straight lines = main beam, not dipped beam

q24201.en: The symbol shown signals that the rear fog light is on.

explain.short: This symbol is the main beam. The rear fog light has a different symbol: a lamp facing the other way with a wavy line across the beams, on an amber light.
explain.rule: Straight lines = main beam (abbaglianti, 'proiettori di profondità'). The symbol is on its switch and on a blue light.
explain.trap: 'luce posteriore per nebbia' (rear fog light) is wrong: there is no wavy fog line here, only straight beams.

sceneParams.caption: Main beam, not the rear fog light

q24202.en: The symbol shown reminds the driver that they must switch off the side lights.

explain.short: The symbol only shows that the main beam is on. It is not a reminder about the side lights (luci di posizione).
explain.rule: Straight lines = main beam (abbaglianti, 'proiettori di profondità'). The symbol is on its switch and on a blue light.
explain.trap: 'ricorda... di spegnere le luci di posizione' is invented: this light just says the main beam is on.

sceneParams.caption: It only shows the main beam is on
lines: Blue light = main beam is on

q24203.en: The symbol shown is on the switch that turns on the dipped beam headlights.

explain.short: A headlamp with lines sloping down towards the road is the dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The beam points down so it does not dazzle others.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'anabbaglianti' is right: lines sloping down = dipped beam; straight lines would be main beam.

sceneParams.caption: Lines sloping down: dipped beam switch
lines: The beam points at the road

q24204.en: The symbol shown is on a green warning light.

explain.short: When the dipped beam is on, a green light with this symbol switches on in the dashboard. Green means a light is working.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'verde' is right here: dipped beam = green; only the main beam is blue.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam on: the warning light is green

q24205.en: The symbol shown is on a blue warning light.

explain.short: This is the dipped beam symbol, and its light is green. Blue is only for the main beam.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'blu' is the trap: blue belongs to the main beam (straight lines), not to the dipped beam.

sceneParams.caption: Not blue: the dipped beam light is green
lines: Its light is GREEN, not blue

q24206.en: The symbol shown signals that the rear fog light is on.

explain.short: This symbol is the dipped beam. The rear fog light has its own symbol, with a wavy line across the beams, on an amber light.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'luce posteriore per nebbia' (rear fog light) is wrong: no wavy fog line here.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam, not the rear fog light

q24207.en: The symbol shown is on the warning light for the main beam being on.

explain.short: The lines slope down, so this is the dipped beam. The main beam symbol has straight lines and a blue light.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'abbaglianti' (main beam) vs 'anabbaglianti' (dipped beam): one letter group changes everything; here the lines slope down.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam, not main beam

q24208.en: The symbol shown signals that the side lights are on.

explain.short: This symbol is the dipped beam. The side lights (luci di posizione) have a different symbol: two small lamps facing outwards.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'luci di posizione' (side lights) is wrong: they have their own symbol, not one big headlamp.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam, not side lights

q24209.en: The symbol shown indicates the control for operating the right direction indicator.

explain.short: This is a headlamp with beams, the dipped beam. The indicators have arrows as their symbol.
explain.rule: Lines sloping down = dipped beam (anabbaglianti). The symbol is on its switch and on a green light.
explain.trap: 'indicatore di direzione destro' (right indicator) is wrong: indicators are shown with arrows, not a headlamp.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam, not the right indicator

q24210.en: The symbol shown indicates the control of the direction indicators.

explain.short: Two arrows, one left and one right, are the symbol of the direction indicators (frecce).
explain.rule: Two arrows = direction indicators. Their light is green and flashes while an indicator is on.
explain.trap: 'indicatori di direzione' are the normal indicators (frecce), one side at a time.

sceneParams.caption: Two arrows: direction indicators
lines: Left or right, one side at a time

q24211.en: The symbol shown is on a green warning light.

explain.short: When an indicator is on, a green arrow flashes in the dashboard. Green means a light is working.
explain.rule: Two arrows = direction indicators. Their light is green and flashes while an indicator is on.
explain.trap: 'verde' is right: the indicator light is green (red is for danger).

sceneParams.caption: Indicator light: green

q24212.en: The symbol shown is on the flashing green warning light of the indicator that is switched on.

explain.short: When you switch on an indicator, the green arrow for that side flashes in the dashboard, together with the indicator outside.
explain.rule: Two arrows = direction indicators. Their light is green and flashes while an indicator is on.
explain.trap: 'lampeggiante' (flashing) is right: the green arrow flashes, it does not stay fixed.

sceneParams.caption: The green arrow flashes with the indicator

q24213.en: The symbol shown is on a red warning light.

explain.short: The indicator light is green, not red. Red lights mean danger, like the hazard lights or the brake warning.
explain.rule: Two arrows = direction indicators. Their light is green and flashes while an indicator is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' is the trap: the normal indicators use a green light.

sceneParams.caption: Not red: the indicator light is green
lines: Their light is GREEN, not red

q24214.en: The symbol shown is on a warning light that comes on when the side lights are on.

explain.short: The arrows only flash when an indicator is working. The side lights have their own symbol.
explain.rule: Two arrows = direction indicators. Their light is green and flashes while an indicator is on.
explain.trap: 'luci di posizione' (side lights) is wrong: arrows mean indicators.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows = indicators, not side lights

q24215.en: The symbol shown indicates the control for switching on the side lights.

explain.short: Two arrows are the direction indicators. The side lights are switched on with another control and symbol.
explain.rule: Two arrows = direction indicators. Their light is green and flashes while an indicator is on.
explain.trap: 'luci di posizione' (side lights) is wrong: the arrows mean indicators.

sceneParams.caption: Indicator control, not side lights

q24216.en: The symbol shown indicates the control for operating the hazard warning lights.

explain.short: The double triangle is the hazard lights button (segnalazione luminosa di pericolo, the 'quattro frecce').
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'segnalazione luminosa di pericolo' means the hazard lights (all indicators flashing).

sceneParams.caption: Double triangle: hazard lights button

q24217.en: The symbol shown is on the control that switches on all the direction indicators at the same time.

explain.short: Pressing the hazard button makes all the indicators (front, back, sides) flash together.
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'contemporanea di tutti' (all at the same time) is exactly what the hazard lights do.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard button: all indicators flash at once

keywords.en: switching on at the same time

q24218.en: The symbol shown is on a red warning light.

explain.short: The hazard lights button with this symbol is red, because it is used for danger. Red = danger.
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'rosso' is right here: the hazard symbol is red, unlike the green indicator arrows.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard symbol: red

q24219.en: The symbol shown indicates a device to be used in emergencies.

explain.short: Hazard lights are for emergencies: for example a vehicle stopped where it is a danger, or a sudden queue ahead.
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'casi di emergenza' (emergencies) is right: that is when you use the hazard lights.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard lights: for emergencies

q24220.en: The symbol shown indicates the control that operates the portable warning sign.

explain.short: The 'segnale mobile di pericolo' is the warning triangle you place on the road by hand. It has no switch; this symbol is the hazard lights.
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'segnale mobile di pericolo' is the warning triangle you put on the road, not the hazard lights.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard lights, not the warning triangle

q24221.en: The symbol shown is on the warning light for the handbrake being on.

explain.short: This is the hazard lights symbol. The handbrake light has a different symbol: a circle with '!' or 'P' inside.
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'freno a mano inserito' (handbrake on) is wrong: that light is a circle, not a triangle.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard lights, not the handbrake

q24222.en: The symbol shown indicates a device that switches on automatically at every accident.

explain.short: The driver switches on the hazard lights by pressing the button. They do not come on by themselves at every accident.
explain.rule: Double triangle = hazard lights (quattro frecce): all indicators flash together. Red switch, for emergencies; you switch it on yourself.
explain.trap: 'automaticamente ad ogni incidente' is the trap: you must press the button yourself.

sceneParams.caption: You switch the hazard lights on yourself

q24223.en: You must use the direction indicators before every lane change when driving on a road divided into lanes.

explain.short: A lane change is a sideways move. The drivers behind and beside you must know it in advance.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'ogni' (every) is right: every lane change needs the indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Every lane change: indicator first

q24224.en: You must use the direction indicators if, driving on a one-way road, you move from the right lane to the left lane.

explain.short: Moving from one lane to another is a lane change, also on a one-way road. Signal left before moving.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' (one-way) changes nothing: a lane change is always signalled.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: signal the lane change too
lines: Right to left lane: signal left

q24225.en: You must use the direction indicators every time you have to make a turn.

explain.short: Every turn, left or right, is a change of direction, so the others must be warned with the indicator.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'ogni volta' (every time) is right: no turn without the indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Every turn: indicator

q24226.en: You must use the direction indicators if you intend to leave the carriageway to stop.

explain.short: Leaving the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles) is a sideways move: signal before pulling off.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'uscire dalla carreggiata' (leave the carriageway) is a change of direction, so the indicator is needed.

sceneParams.caption: Leaving the road to stop: indicator
lines: You want to stop off the road

q24227.en: You must use the direction indicators when, starting from the edge of the carriageway, you want to join the traffic.

explain.short: Pulling out from the edge into the traffic is a sideways move: the drivers coming must see your indicator first.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'immettere nella circolazione' (join the traffic) always needs the indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Pulling out: indicator first

q24228.en: You must use the direction indicators to signal that you intend to move into the deceleration lane of a motorway junction.

explain.short: Moving into the deceleration lane (the exit lane) is a lane change: signal right in good time.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'corsia di decelerazione' (deceleration lane) is the motorway exit lane: you reach it with the indicator on.

sceneParams.caption: Exit lane on the motorway: signal right

q24229.en: You must use the direction indicators to signal that you intend to enter the motorway carriageway, coming from an acceleration lane.

explain.short: From the acceleration lane (the entry lane) you move left into the motorway: signal left before joining.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'corsia di accelerazione' (acceleration lane) is the entry lane: you leave it with the left indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Joining the motorway: signal left

q24230.en: You must not use the direction indicators when you change lane while driving on a one-way road.

explain.short: A lane change must always be signalled, also on a one-way road. Saying you must NOT use them is wrong.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'Non si devono' (you must not) is the trap: on a one-way road you still signal.

sceneParams.caption: One-way road: lane changes are signalled too

q24231.en: It is never necessary to use the direction indicators when driving on a two-way road with carriageways separated by a central reservation.

explain.short: On a divided road you still change lane, turn and exit, and each of these moves needs the indicator.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'Non è mai necessario' (never necessary) is the trap: lane changes and exits are signalled on every road.

sceneParams.caption: Divided road: you still signal every move

q24232.en: You must not use the direction indicators if, to stop off the carriageway, you move to the left edge.

explain.short: Moving to the left edge to stop is a sideways move, so you must signal left. The statement says the opposite.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'Non si devono' plus 'margine sinistro' (left edge): stopping on the left is signalled too.

sceneParams.caption: Stopping on the left: signal left
lines: You stop off the road on the left

q24233.en: You must use the right direction indicators to signal that you are about to brake suddenly.

explain.short: Braking is shown by the brake lights, which come on by themselves. Indicators show a change of direction, not braking.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'per segnalare che si sta per frenare' is the trap: indicators never mean braking.

sceneParams.caption: Brake lights show braking, not indicators

q24234.en: You must not use the direction indicators if you have to turn right to enter a driveway.

explain.short: Entering a driveway (passo carrabile) is a turn, and every turn must be signalled, also to the right.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'Non si devono' is the trap: turning into a 'passo carrabile' (driveway) is a normal turn.

sceneParams.caption: Driveway on the right: signal right

q24235.en: You must use the direction indicators when you turn left, but not when you turn right.

explain.short: Every turn needs the indicator, both left and right. There is no exception for right turns.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'ma non quando si svolta a destra' (but not right) is the trap: right turns are signalled too.

sceneParams.caption: Right turns are signalled too

q24236.en: You must use the left direction indicators when you have to drive along a hairpin bend to the left.

explain.short: A hairpin bend (tornante) is just the road bending sharply. You follow your road, you do not turn off it, so no indicator.
explain.rule: Signal every sideways move in good time: lane changes, turns, pulling out, pulling off the road, motorway entry and exit. Indicators show direction, not braking.
explain.trap: 'tornante' (hairpin bend) is a curve of the same road, not a turn.

sceneParams.caption: Following a bend is not a turn: no indicator
lines: You stay on the same road

q24237.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary to signal that you want to change lane.

explain.short: A lane change is a sideways move. Signal it so the drivers around you know.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'necessario' (necessary) is right: lane changes always need the indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Lane change: indicator needed

q24238.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary to signal the intention to overtake.

explain.short: To overtake you move out to the left: signal left before you start.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'sorpasso' (overtaking) starts with a move to the left, so the indicator is needed.

sceneParams.caption: Overtaking: signal left first

q24239.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary to signal the intention to park on the left edge of a one-way road.

explain.short: On a one-way road you may park on the left. Moving to the left edge is a sideways move: signal left.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'margine sinistro' (left edge) is fine on a one-way road, and it is signalled with the left indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Parking on the left: signal left
lines: Left indicator, then park on the left

q24240.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary every time you have to make a turn.

explain.short: Every turn changes your direction, so it must always be signalled.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'ogni qualvolta' (every time) is right: no exceptions for turns.

sceneParams.caption: Every turn: indicator

q24241.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary when reversing.

explain.short: Reversing is a risky move that changes your position on the road. Show the others which way you are going with the indicator.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'retromarcia' (reversing) is a manoeuvre too, so the indicator is needed.

sceneParams.caption: Reversing: signal with the indicator

q24242.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary when driving in parallel lines of traffic, even if you do not change lane.

explain.short: In parallel lines of traffic (marcia per file parallele) you just stay in your lane. With no change of lane, there is nothing to signal.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'anche se non si effettuano cambiamenti di corsia' (even without changing lane) is the trap: no move, no indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Staying in your lane: no indicator

q24243.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary for at least 500 metres after overtaking.

explain.short: The indicator is used only during the move. Once you are back in your lane, you switch it off.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'almeno 500 metri' (at least 500 metres) is invented: no such rule exists.

sceneParams.caption: Indicator off once the move is over

q24244.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary when you start an overtake, but not when you finish it by moving back into your normal lane.

explain.short: Overtaking has two sideways moves: out to the left and back to the right. Both must be signalled.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'ma non quando la si termina' (but not when you finish) is the trap: signal right when moving back too.

sceneParams.caption: Signal when moving out AND when moving back

keywords.it: ma non quando la si termina
keywords.en: but not when you finish it

q24245.en: Using the direction indicators is not necessary if you have to park the vehicle by moving to the right edge of the carriageway.

explain.short: Moving to the right edge to park is a sideways move: signal right. Others behind you must know you are pulling in.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'non è necessario' (not necessary) is the trap: parking on the right needs the indicator too.

sceneParams.caption: Parking on the right: signal right
lines: You pull in to park on the right

q24246.en: Using the direction indicators is necessary when you stop at a red traffic light.

explain.short: At a red light you just stop in your lane. You do not change direction, so no indicator is needed for stopping.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'quando ci si arresta ad un semaforo rosso' (stopping at a red light): stopping is not a change of direction.

sceneParams.caption: Stopping at a red light: no indicator
lines: Red light: you stop in your lane

q24247.en: Using the right direction indicators is necessary when you stop because the traffic is blocked.

explain.short: If traffic stops ahead you simply stop in your lane. The right indicator would wrongly say you are moving right.
explain.rule: Indicators are for changes of direction or lane, from the start to the end of the move. Standing still in your lane needs no indicator.
explain.trap: 'indicatori di direzione destri' (right indicators) is the trap: you are not moving right, you are just stopping.

sceneParams.caption: Stopped in a queue: no right indicator

q24248.en: Using the main beam headlights is, as a rule, forbidden while driving in built-up areas.

explain.short: In towns the streets are lit and there are many people, so main beam would dazzle them. As a rule you use dipped beam.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) makes it true: in towns, the normal rule is no main beam.

sceneParams.caption: In towns: no main beam, as a rule
lines: In town: lit streets, many people

q24249.en: Using the main beam headlights is necessary outside built-up areas when street lighting is insufficient and you are not meeting other vehicles.

explain.short: Outside towns in poor light you need to see far ahead. With nobody coming the other way, main beam dazzles no one.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'insufficiente' (insufficient) and 'non si incrociano' (no oncoming vehicles) together make main beam the right choice.

sceneParams.caption: Outside town, poor light, nobody coming: main beam

keywords.en: you are not meeting other vehicles

q24250.en: Using the main beam headlights is necessary outside built-up areas when there is no street lighting and you are not meeting other vehicles.

explain.short: Outside towns with no street lights it is dark, and you must see far. With no oncoming vehicles, use main beam.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'manca' (is missing) and 'non si incrociano' (no oncoming vehicles): both conditions are there, so main beam is right.

sceneParams.caption: Outside town, no lights, nobody coming: main beam

keywords.en: you are not meeting other vehicles

q24251.en: Using the main beam headlights must be replaced by using the dipped beam headlights when meeting other vehicles.

explain.short: Main beam dazzles the drivers coming the other way. When you meet a vehicle, switch to dipped beam.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'incrociano' (meet, oncoming) is the key: oncoming vehicle = dipped beam.

sceneParams.caption: Vehicle coming: switch to dipped beam
lines: A car comes the other way

q24252.en: Using the main beam headlights is, as a rule, allowed in town in thick fog.

explain.short: In fog the strong main beam reflects back off the fog and blinds you. Also, in towns main beam is not used as a rule.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'consentito... in caso di nebbia fitta' is the trap: fog is the worst moment for main beam.

sceneParams.caption: Fog: main beam blinds you, use dipped beam

q24253.en: Using the main beam headlights is necessary in one-way urban tunnels.

explain.short: In tunnels you must use the dipped beam. Main beam is not required there, and in towns it is not used as a rule.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'necessario' (necessary) is the trap: in tunnels the compulsory light is the dipped beam.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel: dipped beam, not main beam

q24254.en: Using the main beam headlights is always allowed when carrying injured or seriously ill people.

explain.short: Carrying injured people does not change the light rules. Main beam can still dazzle others, so no exception.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'sempre ammesso' (always allowed) is the trap: there is no special rule for carrying the injured.

sceneParams.caption: Injured on board: same light rules

q24255.en: Using the main beam headlights is necessary by day if you drive on a motorway against the sun.

explain.short: Main beam is for the dark, not for daytime. Driving against the sun, it would only dazzle others; slow down and use the sun visor.
explain.rule: Main beam: outside towns, in the dark, with nobody to dazzle. Meeting another vehicle: switch to dipped beam. In towns, as a rule, no.
explain.trap: 'di giorno' (by day) and 'controsole' (against the sun) are the trap: main beam does not help against the sun.

sceneParams.caption: By day against the sun: no main beam
lines: Use the sun visor, slow down
